lessons.key: surviving_mutant::when an idempotency guard uses a strict inequality to reject duplicate out of order events e g where applied incoming add a test case for the exact equality boundary not just the strictly less than case or a mutation survives silently
lessons.text: When an idempotency guard uses a strict inequality to reject duplicate/out-of-order events (e.g. WHERE applied < incoming), add a test case for the exact-equality boundary, not just the strictly-less-than case, or a </<= mutation survives silently.

lessons.key: surviving_mutant::when classifying a domain exception as non retryable for a message broker retry interceptor add an end to end test that triggers that exact exception type through the real listener and broker not only a unit test of the exception being thrown or a retry policy misclassification for that type survives undetected
lessons.text: When classifying a domain exception as non-retryable for a message broker retry interceptor, add an end-to-end test that triggers that exact exception type through the real listener and broker, not only a unit test of the exception being thrown, or a retry-policy misclassification for that type survives undetected.

lessons.key: gate_fail::when naming integration test classes with the it suffix bind maven failsafe plugin to the integration test verify phases because maven surefire s default test goal does not match it java and mvn test silently reports success while skipping all it coverage
lessons.text: When naming integration test classes with the *IT suffix, bind maven-failsafe-plugin to the integration-test/verify phases, because Maven Surefire's default test goal does not match *IT.java and mvn test silently reports success while skipping all IT coverage.

lessons.key: spec_precision_gap::when an ac s when clause lists multiple distinct triggering sub cases e g sem set local definido ou com o tenant errado write one test per sub case not just the easiest one to simulate since the untested sub case can behave differently error vs empty result than assumed
lessons.text: When an AC's WHEN-clause lists multiple distinct triggering sub-cases (e.g. 'sem SET LOCAL definido, ou com o tenant errado'), write one test per sub-case, not just the easiest one to simulate, since the untested sub-case can behave differently (error vs empty result) than assumed.
